statement: Every number in this file is a declaration to be tested by docs/EXPERIMENTS.md; none is derived by the engine and none is a law of nature.

The catalog is exactly two things: the rays of nature, with the couplings that say what happens when ray A meets ray B, a table; and the apparatus, the Detector and the external body, the declarations an experimenter places on the board that obey no table.
The engine only reads this file: a world file selects rays from it and places apparatus, and nothing else exists on the board (Highlights 3.26, 3.30).

A value the model owner has not decided is the string "undecided", beside a decided_by that names the experiment (docs/EXPERIMENTS.md) or the hypothesis (docs/HYPOTHESES.md) that decides it; nothing is invented in its place.
Every value is an exact integer or a ratio [n, d] of exact integers; there are no floats. JSON has no comments, so a note key carries the explanation.

Under the law of the bit (Highlights 5.4, the model owner, 2026-09-18; the cleanup of the same day) there is no field family: a shadow is a ray of its owner's family with the bit 0, every ray record is a family of things, its shadow set the release ratio it declares, and the phase circle is one for the world, N, declared once beside K.

content.note: The content of the electron, one quantum, the unit of the mass ladder (hypotheses 12 and 14): a thing's content is its mass and its clock (Highlights 5.4 point 19, clock-readings-v1, 2026-09-18): a thing of a family that declares clock advances its phase by content / K steps per interval, K the world's one integer (the world key K), the remainder kept exactly on the thing; every content on the ladder is an integer number of quanta, light has no clock, and no family declares a rest rate (the former kerengonen.phase_advance is refused). The world keys are clock on the family and K on the world.

charge.note: Every charge is an integer number of thirds of the elementary charge e, so that quarks are integers (up +2, down -1) and the electron is -3; the charge of the things summed over the rays of a meeting is an invariant the engine appends to every coupling (wave-ray-family-v1). The world key is charge, the charge of one thing of the family, whole, whatever its content (Highlights 5.4 point 16 as amended, the model owner, 2026-09-18; charge-per-thing-v1): an electron of 64 quanta is -3 as the electron of 1 is, never a charge per quantum; a thing multiplies an electric message by it whole, and its shadows carry its charge over its content as their message.

phase.note: A phase is an integer from 0 below N, the number of steps of the phase circle, one for the world like K (Highlights 5.4, the definitions of the law, the model owner, 2026-09-18): declared once as the world key N, 64 by default, a power of two from 2 through 4096; an advance and a difference are masks with N - 1, never a division. A phase difference between any two rays, of one family or of two, is read on the one circle, so a width per family means nothing: the per-family phase_bits of the engine and of this file are retired in the cleanup of 2026-09-18. The steering table of two things of one family that meet is computed from N (point 17), and the Node's mixing of shadows reads N (point 24); the register's boards ran at 256 steps and the reference Born table is written at 8, both declared as N.

amount.note: The content of a ray, a bounded integer; the energy of the invariants is the amount, the momentum is amount x heading.

light.note: The electromagnetic quantum as a family of things (Highlights 3.5 and 5.4 point 12, the model owner, 2026-09-17 and 2026-09-18): a photon is one quantum of it, emitted at an event by any source, a lamp or an atom, and absorbed at its meeting with a bound group or at a mark; light is the field of nothing and no family is its field. No mass and no charge (Highlights 3.3): no clock (clock false), so a ray carries the phase of the clock that emitted it, the emitter's at emission, and delivers it unchanged, and the frequency of light is its emitter's rate (point 19: a photon emitted at a transition carries the emitter's change of content and beats at the emitter's change of rate, E = h nu). The field of a charge is not this family: under the law of the bit the field of an electron is the electron's own shadows, rays of the electron family with the bit 0, given with the board (initial_field) and circulating, their set the release of the electron's record; the light family's own shadow set (whether a photon's content casts a shadow read by gravity) is undecided, hypothesis 17's, and until then a world declares no release on light. The families electron_field and positron_field of 2026-09-17, then light as a field family with field_of and source_sign, are retired: a shadow carries its owner's charge sign and content as its message, set by the engine, and the sign is no declaration of this file. Polarization (feature 11, Highlights 3.26; decided by A12 on 2026-09-17, ray-polarization-v1): the polarization entry transverse says that every light ray carries a transverse direction modulo a half turn, an integer step of a circle of 2^polarization_bits steps per half turn (the world key polarization_bits on the family, the world's phase circle by default, default here), or none for an unpolarized ray; 0 is the first transverse lattice axis of the ray's heading (+Y for a ray on +X) and half the circle the second (+Z), which are the two states of Highlights 3.26, and the steps between them are the transverse direction 3.26 allows for the circular case, without the handedness bit, which no ray carries. A lamp declares the polarization of what it emits (the world key polarization on the emission); rays merge only at equal polarization; a meeting's outputs carry their source input's unless the output declares one; the return keeps it; the engine reads it nowhere but at the polarizer coupling and in a coupling's guard. A12 confronted it with Malus's law and the three-polarizer chain on 2026-09-17 (its entry holds the numbers): the intermediate polarizer's angle is carried through the chain, since the property is the direction and not one of two states. Two things of this family meeting on one lane are one ray of many quanta (Highlights 5.4 point 25: light has no bound).

reference.note: the register's value for A9; a measured number for comparison, not a lattice value

electron.note: Content 1, the unit m_0 (hypotheses 12 and 14; Highlights 5.4 point 19, clock-readings-v1): its mass and its clock are its content, content / K phase steps per interval at the world's K. Charge -1 e, that is -3 in thirds. Its field is its own shadow set (Highlights 5.4 point 12, the law of the bit, 2026-09-18): rays of this family with the bit 0, carrying its identity, charge and content as their message, given with the board and circulating, their set release times its content per heading (the ratio the electric runs declare; A5 confronts it with Coulomb's law); gravity and electricity are that one shadow set read twice (point 18), times the content of what is pushed (reads content) and times the owner's charge over its content times the charge of what is pushed (reads charge); light, the family electron_field of 2026-09-17 and the mass field are no longer its field. A10 decides whether the electron is the first rung of the ladder at the real N; until then every other content is written as a multiple of the electron's. Spin, the two-state polarization of the electron family (feature 11, ray-polarization-v1, 2026-09-17), is the same ray property as light's polarization at one bit, polarization_bits 1 (the world key on the family): the steps 0 and 1, or none; the engine gives it no other meaning, and it is read only by pauli_exclusion, whose table the composite spectrum of hypothesis 12 decides, which is what spin stands undecided for.

positron.note: The electron's antiparticle: the same content and clock, charge +1 e, that is +3 in thirds, spin the same property at one bit; its field is its own shadow set, read as the electron's (Highlights 5.4 points 12, 16 and 18, the law of the bit, 2026-09-18), so the attraction of opposite charges is the product of the two charges in the electricity reading and no separate declaration.

muon.note: A charged ray of the electron's kind on a higher rung of the ladder: its rest rate is k x 206.768 28 for the electron's rung k, and A10 finds the smallest k at which the muon, tau and proton ratios are all integers at one N (hypothesis 12); the ladder value is undecided until then. No entry of the register places a muon ray on a board, so its field, light as for every charge (Highlights 3.5, 2026-09-17), and its couplings are declared in its record when one does; its mass field is declared because it is massive.

neutrino.note: A neutral ray. On the ladder its rest rate is an integer number of steps like every rest mass, and no entry of the register fixes its rung; it joins the field_of list of mass_field when its rest rate is declared nonzero. No coupling of the register reads a neutrino.

antineutrino.note: The neutrino's antiparticle, the third product of weak_conversion (A9): A9 holds energy and momentum exact at the conversion, which bounds its rung without deciding it.

colour.note: a property of the ray with three values, set by the world per ray and read only at a meeting by quark_binding and gluon_gluon_binding; no engine rule reads it (Highlights 3.26); catalog work after feature 10

up.note: A quark family (Highlights 3.26): charge +2/3 e, that is +2 in thirds; colour a property with three values; its field is its own shadow set (Highlights 5.4 point 12, 2026-09-18: the strong field of a quark is the quark's shadows, of this family with the bit 0), and the gluon is a family of real rays it emits at events (Highlights 3.26 as amended); the size of its shadow set is hypothesis 17's. Its rung on the ladder is a catalog value that hypothesis 12 leaves to the composite spectrum.

down.note: A quark family: charge -1/3 e, that is -1 in thirds; colour as for up; its field is its own shadow set (Highlights 5.4 point 12, 2026-09-18: the strong field of a quark is the quark's shadows, of this family with the bit 0), and the gluon is a family of real rays it emits at events (Highlights 3.26 as amended); the size of its shadow set is hypothesis 17's. Its rung on the ladder is left to the composite spectrum of hypothesis 12.

gluon.note: A family of real rays with colour charge, emitted at events as light is (Highlights 3.26 as amended by the model owner on 2026-09-18, under the law of the bit): there is no field family, so the strong field of a quark is the quark's own shadows (Highlights 5.4, point 12), and the gluon is a family of things, bit 1, differing from light in that it carries colour charge and so is itself pushed. No content on the ladder and no clock, like light: a gluon carries the phase of the event that emitted it. How a gluon ray carries its colour (colour, a property of the ray with three values, read only at a meeting, or one family per colour) and the size of its own shadow set (release: whether and how a gluon's content casts a shadow) are hypothesis 13's declarations, written before its run; the binding of gluon rays to each other is gluon_gluon_binding, the string of E7, and the field between quarks that closes into loops of gluon rays is read with the gluon as a thing family. What fixes a shadow set's size, the symmetry of Highlights 3.27 and the path counting of 3.5, or nothing, is hypothesis 17 (Highlights 5.5, 2026-09-17); until it is answered the ratio is an input and the model predicts the form 1/r^2, not the value of the coupling. The gluon entry as a field family (kind field, field_of up and down) is retired.

reference.note: the register's value for A9; the ratio to the electron, 1836.152 67, is the one A10 fits

proton.note: Matter (Highlights 3.4): two up and one down quark rays on a ring of Nodes under quark_binding (since 2026-09-17 a corner table, loop-binding-v1; held at one Node under the interim form before), colour-neutral, charge +3 in thirds (+1 e). Its rest rate is its retained content, the ladder rung A10 fits; its field is its own shadow set (Highlights 5.4 points 12 and 18, 2026-09-18), read twice, for gravity times the content of what is pushed and for electricity times its charge over its content times the charge of what is pushed; light and the mass field are no longer its fields, and gluons are emitted at the events of its members. In A8 it stands as an external body of this family, charge +3, amount M_p, radiating light; when its recoil is wanted it is this bound group. No coupling converts it: the proton is stable.

neutron.note: Matter: one up and two down quark rays on a ring of Nodes under quark_binding (since 2026-09-17 a corner table, loop-binding-v1), colour-neutral, charge 0. Its rest rate is its retained content, the composite spectrum of hypothesis 12; A9 runs its decay and A14 may run it as the moving bound group. Its field is its own shadow set, read by gravity alone since its charge is 0 (Highlights 5.4 points 12 and 18, 2026-09-18), its size hypothesis 17's; gluons are emitted at the events of its members, as for the proton. Its decay is a table on weak_conversion, not a draw (Highlights 5.4 point 20, clock-readings-v1, 2026-09-18).

born_steering.table_rule: the table is not declared (the model owner, 2026-09-18, Highlights 5.4 point 17): the engine writes it once from the family's phase width N as cos^2(d/2) in N-ths, rounded to the nearest whole, for d the phase difference of the two rays; [8, 7, 4, 1, 0, 1, 4, 7] at N = 8 (Highlights 3.3; ray-event model, step 6), the shadows' spread is the Node's mixing and reads no table (feature 16c, Highlights 5.4 point 24); the catalog declares only which pairs steer
born_steering.note: Interference as steering (Highlights 3.3): where two rays of one family meet in one layer, the coupling reads their phase difference d and splits the shared content between the two candidate Ports in the ratio table[d] : N - table[d], the table output taking floor(content x table[d] / N) and the rest output the rest, so the remainder has an owner (3.17); nothing is erased and no Detector reads it. The two Ports here, +Y and -Y, are the world's choice; the same table serves any family whose rays meet in one layer (A1 confronts the electron fringes of Tonomura as well as light). Charge x amount is appended as an invariant by the engine.

engine.identity: ray-momentum-turn-v3 under bit-law-v1 and clock-readings-v1 (a momentum table with its reading)

electron_field_turn.note: Repulsion through the field, under the law of the bit (Highlights 5.4 points 3, 15, 16 and 18, the model owner, 2026-09-18): an electron that meets a shadow of another electron takes the push the table declares, sign 1 (repulsion) times the shadow's amount times its heading, read times the owner's charge over its content times the electron's own charge (reads charge, point 16), added to its momentum; the shadow turns back with the opposite sign carrying -push, a field like any other from then on (point 3, return-field-v1), and is absorbed wherever it reaches its owner, whose momentum takes what it carries: the third law holds through the field. The same family on both sides: the shadow is an electron with the bit 0, so one line of this file covers the electron's field and no field family is named; a positron meeting an electron's shadow is the same table with the product of the charges negative, attraction, which is the former opposite_charge entry closed by the reading of point 16 (A5 confronts the whole). The declared integer table over the arriving field content and the charge product (strength_table) is the size of the shadow set, release on the family, and is written before A5's run. The outputs form of 2026-09-17 (the electron leaving whole on the field ray's heading, the field ray returned reversed as a fresh event ray) and the momentum_table over a light family are retired with the field family.

engine.identity: loop-binding-v1: ray-meeting-conversion-v1, an outputs rule whose loop closes

electron_proton_binding.closes: the Port form of the corner table (docs/LOOP_BINDING.md, section 2): at a corner each input leaves through the Port the other came in by, with its own amount and phase, so on a ring an electron ray circulating one way and a proton ray the other are back at every corner in the same state; closure is the presence of a partner at every corner, the headings by the ring's geometry, every amount under this form, and the phase closing on the circle, L r = 0 (mod N) per family in one circuit (docs/LOOP_BINDING.md, section 3); this form gives no content ladder, which is A8's, and the electron's meetings with the proton's own field rays (electron_field_turn) are the open closure the ladder needs
electron_proton_binding.note: Matter as a bound group (Highlights 3.4): the electron ray around a proton, on a ring of Nodes, its meetings with the proton reproducing the rays that entered them. Whether bound trajectories exist only at discrete retained energies, and their ladder (the Balmer ratio 27/5), is what A8 decides; nothing states a level structure. Unbinding is an arriving light ray of content at least the binding (A8's second series): a ray arriving at a corner is met by the table declared for the families present, and its outputs leave the ring or join it. Written as a corner table on 2026-09-17 (feature 14, loop-binding-v1): the held delay-1 form of ray-binding-v1, with its ray_delay wait, is gone from the engine; a binding coupling is an ordinary meeting table whose loop closes, the electron's meetings with the proton reproduce the rays that entered them on a ring of Nodes, and the ladder A8 decides is the set of loop-closing contents, which the Port form does not restrict (docs/LOOP_BINDING.md, section 7).

engine.identity: loop-binding-v1 with three participants and the colour property (catalog work after feature 10)

quark_binding.guard: the three colours differ (the group is colour-neutral)
quark_binding.closes: a corner table over three quark rays, an outputs rule whose loop closes: which contents and phases of three rays on a ring reproduce themselves under it is the composite spectrum of hypothesis 12, counted as A10 counts (docs/LOOP_BINDING.md, section 7)
quark_binding.note: The strong binding (Highlights 3.4, 3.26): three quark rays, one of each colour, circulating on a ring of Nodes and meeting again in the same state, their corner table reproducing the rays that entered it. The proton and the neutron are its bound groups; which combinations stay bound and what they retain is the composite spectrum of hypothesis 12, its first targets the lightest cases; A9 and A14 run its groups. Written as a corner table on 2026-09-17 (feature 14, loop-binding-v1): the held form at one Node is gone from the engine, this is an ordinary meeting table whose loop closes, its outputs undecided, and the composite spectrum of hypothesis 12 is the set of loops the table closes.

engine.identity: loop-binding-v1 on gluon rays, with the colour of hypothesis 13

gluon_gluon_binding.closes: a corner table over two gluon rays, an outputs rule whose loop closes along the line between two quarks: the string of E7; which patterns close under it is hypothesis 13's
gluon_gluon_binding.note: The quark's field rays binding to each other (Highlights 3.26; hypothesis 13): one more declared coupling from which the short range of the strong interaction and its growth with distance are expected. Whether it yields confinement is a research question for that run, not an engine decision; the table is written before it. Written as a corner table on 2026-09-17 (feature 14, loop-binding-v1): an ordinary meeting table whose loop closes, its outputs undecided; the held form is gone from the engine. In the language of binding as a loop (Highlights 3.26, 2026-09-17): the strong field differs from light by one catalog line, its rays couple to each other, so the field between quarks does not spread as a sphere but closes into loops of gluon rays along the line between them, a string whose content, and so whose mass, grows with the distance; only colour-neutral patterns close a loop, which is confinement as a closure condition; and a string stretched to the content at which a new loop closes with a quark and an antiquark breaks into two hadrons, which is hadronization; nothing inserted, hypothesis 13 in the research run E7 after feature 14.

engine.identity: ray-meeting-conversion-v1 with the decay table of clock-readings-v1 (landed 2026-09-18) at a corner meeting of the neutron's ring (quark_binding, loop-binding-v1, not landed)

weak_conversion.fires: at a corner meeting of the group's rays when the declared condition on the group's state is met (Highlights 5.4 point 20, clock-readings-v1, 2026-09-18): the rule declares decay {"after_periods": n} (the group breaks at its n-th meeting under the rule, its passages counted on its rays) or {"content_at_most": c}; nothing is drawn, no counter and no ticket; until 2026-09-18 the rule drew with a setting [n, d] at every corner meeting (decay-draw-v1), and before that a mark on the group's Node drew
weak_conversion.note: The weak interaction as a change of family: an N-to-M conversion at an event (Highlights 3.26), neutron to proton + electron + antineutrino, the group's members going from up 1, down 2 to up 2, down 1, with charge (0 = +3 - 3 + 0), amount and momentum exact. A free particle never decays: the neutron is a bound group whose ticks are events, and it breaks when the declared condition on its own state is met, its n-th meeting under the rule (after_periods, A9's declaration) or its content at most c; there is no lottery (Highlights 5.4 points 14 and 20). A9 pins the survival curve (1 - n/d)^t, one conversion per group, the electron's energy at most 782 keV and no proton group ever firing; the shares of the neutron's content among the three products and their headings are written before that run. The charge invariant is the one the engine appends; it is written here because it is the point of the conversion. In the loop form as implemented (clock-readings-v1, 2026-09-18): the condition is read at every corner meeting of the ring's rays under this rule, declared before the corner table, and whether a population of identical groups decays by the exponential law is a question of their histories and their phases at birth (A9); the outputs may change family, the change booked as each family's source; the neutron's ring under quark_binding is not yet declared.

engine.identity: loop-binding-v1 with the spin property of feature 11

pauli_exclusion.guard: does not fire for two electrons in the same state with the same spin
pauli_exclusion.closes: a corner table over two electron rays of one family, the Born form named by the design (docs/LOOP_BINDING.md, section 3, item 6: born_steering at the corner, closing at equal amounts with the senses a quarter turn apart, d = N/4 or 3N/4, and dispersing in phase), with the guard on spin; what two electrons of opposite spin bind to is hypothesis 12's
pauli_exclusion.note: Pauli exclusion is a binding coupling that does not fire for two electrons in the same state with the same spin (Highlights 3.26); after feature 11, polarization. Its table, what two electrons of opposite spin bind to, is decided with the composite spectrum of hypothesis 12. Written as a corner table on 2026-09-17 (feature 14, loop-binding-v1): an ordinary meeting table whose loop closes, its outputs undecided; the held form is gone from the engine.

engine.identity: ray-meeting-conversion-v1 with the delay output of a meeting (an output-clock wait), where a transmission of inverse-split-v1 catches its share

transmission_meets_held_share.note: A3: the transmission returned through the birth event by Alice's Detector meets Bob's share, waiting under a delay output beyond the round trip; the coupling between the transmission and the waiting ray is a declared table, and since loop-binding-v1 (2026-09-17) a ray waiting at its event Node is met by nothing there, so where the two meet is A3's to write with the table; written before the run, whose exact expectation on the 256-step circle (724/256 at the singlet settings) is computed before it (hypothesis 11, line 2). The two rays are siblings of one event and the transmission carries the bit; the coupling reads only what a coupling reads.

absorber.note: The default coupling of an external body (Highlights 3.19), the world's coupling value "sink": whatever arrives, outbound or returning, ends in the body's exact sink counter for its family in its arrival interval, so a wall, a screen and a beam stop are this; the audit books it on the absorbed_by_bodies line (initial + sources = current + dissipated + escaped + annulled + absorbed_by_bodies at every completed tick), and a field ray of a family the body's momentum_table names moves the body by the table. Matter that arrives gives no push.

mirror.note: A reversed heading (Highlights 3.19): the arriving ray leaves on the negation of its heading with its amount and phase, the body's token returned unchanged as the second output; the reflection is one event (ray-event-state-v1) whose record counts the token as one quantum on +X, and the momentum it turns is booked at the meeting as for any meeting. A2's arms and the light clock of the ray-event model use it.

first.heading: the first declared Port
first.amount: by the table at the phase difference between the arriving ray and the body's token, the body's phase

beam_splitter.note: A split by a declared table between two Ports (Highlights 3.19), the engine's table split indexed by the phase difference of two inputs, here the arriving ray and the body's token, the remainder owned by the second output (3.17); the ratio is A2's declaration, written before its run. A2 places one at the head of each arm, its two outputs the long and the short path.

phase_plate.setting: the body's declared offset, an integer below N, switched by the world per pair (A2: Alice 0 and 64, Bob 32 and 96 at N = 256)
phase_plate.note: A phase offset (Highlights 3.19): the arriving ray continues with its amount and heading and its phase plus the setting, read modulo N, the body's token returned unchanged as the second output. A2 and A3 place one on the long path of each arm; it is the Bell setting in phase form (hypothesis 11). Under lanes-v1 (Highlights 5.4, point 25, 2026-09-18) the token, written on the ray's own heading, shares its lane, and the departure is refused until bodies are things with their own line (the cleanup of 2026-09-18 pins the refusal; the coordinator holds the question of #293).

outputs.shape: the arriving light ray re-emitted over the forward headings (the Ports that do not lead back) with its phase unchanged, one event, the body's token returned unchanged

slit.note: A1: each slit is a declared catalog coupling that re-emits the arriving light ray over the forward headings with its phase unchanged; the share per heading is written before the run. The two slit rays then meet at each screen Node under born_steering. With feature 12, field spreading (Highlights 3.5, 2026-09-17), light spreads by the split table of its own family and a slit is a gap in a wall that absorbs, needing no rule of its own; this coupling stands until then.

sink.amount: floor(amount x (D - T[d]) / D), into the body's sink counter

outputs.remainder: the two shares below one quantum, one quantum in total or none, into the body's pass and sink registers per source sign, in D-ths, each released whole through its output when it reaches D
outputs.difference: d = (angle - polarization) mod D, D = 2^polarization_bits the steps of the polarized family's circle per half turn
outputs.rule: T[d] = round(D cos^2(d x 180 / D degrees)), the reference table at three bits; a world writes its own D entries
outputs.unpolarized: the table's mean, sum(T) / D, unless the body declares unpolarized

polarizer.note: A polarization read (Highlights 3.19, 3.26; decided by A12 on 2026-09-17, feature 11): the arriving content of the polarized family is split between the pass Port and the body's sink by the declared table at the difference between the body's angle and the ray's polarization, cos^2(theta - theta_ray) in D-ths, rounded, the pass share leaving as a fresh event ray with the body's angle as its polarization and the ray's phase, bit and sign, the rest into the body's sink counter (the absorbed_by_bodies line), and the remainder below one quantum owned by the body's registers exactly as a spread's is owned by the Node's (field-remainder-v1). It is declared on the body (world keys: coupling polarizer, and polarizer {family, angle, pass, table, unpolarized}), not as a rule over a token: its rest ends in a counter and its remainder in registers, which the rule form (rays in, rays out, exact over rays) cannot say, so no token is needed. A12 measured on 2026-09-17: a two-state property does not describe it; the property is the direction, the intermediate polarizer's angle is carried through the chain, and the chain y, 45, 90 passes a quarter. A13 uses it as the Bell setting; the two-channel form A13 names, the rejected share leaving on a second Port instead of sinking, is not declared here.

layers.note: Derived, never declared (ray-layers-v1; Highlights 5.1): the layers are the connected components of the rays over the participants of the couplings; a ray that no coupling names is its own layer and crosses everything. The runner records them per world as ray_layer_families.

engine.identity: detector-mark-v1, with detector-return-v1, inverse-split-v1, detector-absorb-v1, bit-law-v1 and node-is-ports-v1

declaration.position: the marked Node, one mark per position
declaration.setting: [n, d], the mark's table, 1 <= d, 0 <= n <= d: the k-th thing to arrive is caught when k mod d < n, else returned on its steps to its birth event (bit-law-v1, point 14: no lottery); 1 catches every thing, 0 returns every arrival; a shadow is always returned and never counted
declaration.on_click: optional, "absorb" (the default for every family) or "pass", for every ray family or as a mapping of ray family name to one of them: the declared table of the thing resident at the mark, what it does with a thing the mark catches (the coupling on_click below)

detector.does: It is a Node whose Detector bit is set, and what it holds is a thing resident at it (Highlights 5.4, point 22, node-is-ports-v1; the law of the bit, bit-law-v1): a thing that arrives is caught by the mark's table, the k-th arrival when k mod d < n, and the click is an absorption into the resident thing, whose content grows by the absorbed amount and whose momentum by the absorbed momentum (booked on the audit as absorbed by marks, the click recording the amount), unless the resident's table on_click says pass for its family, when the thing walks on with its bit; a thing the table misses is returned on its line, back the steps it has made, to its birth event, where it performs the inverse split of its share (a seeded thing leaves its seed Node again on its original heading, settled rule (iii)). A shadow that arrives is returned on its steps without a draw and without a count, a mark counts nothing of a field (point 6), unless the resident is its home: a shadow of a thing the mark absorbed is absorbed into the resident on its shadows line, with the momentum it carries, and makes no event (settled rule (iv)). There is no draw, no seed and no counter: the only uncertainty is whether a 0 or a 1 arrives (point 8), and the resident is the record of what the mark has absorbed, per bit and per family, with its momentum and the identities it is made of.

values.absorb: the thing ends in the thing resident at the mark, on its things line with its momentum, booked as absorbed by marks; the click records the absorbed amount and nothing of the thing is delivered to the Node (the default for every family, bit-law-v1)
values.pass: the thing continues with its bit 1 as at an unmarked Node, the click of detector-mark-v1

on_click.alternative: the other value, per family or for every family
on_click.note: What a marked Node does with a thing it catches (Highlights 5.4, A click is an absorption, model owner, 2026-09-18; landed 2026-09-18 as feature 2c of issue #169, restated under bit-law-v1 and node-is-ports-v1): the thing a marked Node realizes ends there, absorbed into the thing resident at the mark, a photon detected by being absorbed and every measurement paid; a counter that lets a family through writes on_click {"light": "pass"} on its detectors[] entry. Decided on the loop screen (E9, 2026-09-17): with the clicked quantum spreading on, its bit left the marks along the screen and the screen stopped clicking at tick 72; a screen that absorbs counts, and its count grows as an intensity (E9 repeated under the rule on 2026-09-18).

detector.note: A source is a thing that spends its content by its emission table (Highlights 5.4, point 22): a lamp burns content, nothing is injected and nothing is sourced; the marked Node of the earlier form is no longer required of a source. A bound group that can decay breaks by a declared condition on its own state, a table (point 20). A passive Recorder or Renderer is not a Detector.

declaration.position: the Node that holds all of it; one body per Node, never on a Detector
declaration.family: a ray id of this catalog, or the apparatus family below
declaration.amount: a positive integer of any width: the body's content, entering no sum (it releases nothing: its shadows are given with the board, bit-law-v1)
declaration.charge: optional, in thirds of e, the body's whole charge, what it multiplies an electric message by (charge-per-thing-v1) and, over its amount, the message its shadows carry
declaration.phase: optional, the phase its shadows carry, below the world's N; 0 by default
declaration.initial_momentum: optional, a unit-axial heading and a pace [n, d] of Links per interval, n at most d; the momentum is the whole quanta of amount x n / d on that axis; absent for a body at rest
declaration.coupling: optional, "sink" (the default, the absorber below), "polarizer" (with the polarizer declaration below) or the name of a declared coupling below
declaration.momentum_table: optional, family id to sign: -1 attraction toward the owner of an arriving shadow of that family (a shadow is a ray of its owner's family with the bit 0), 1 repulsion; the shadow pushes the body and turns back with the opposite sign carrying the opposite momentum, a field from then on (bit-law-v1, point 3 as amended; return-field-v1)
declaration.reads: with momentum_table: "content" or "charge", what the body multiplies the shadows' message by (bit-law-v1, point 16)
declaration.thing: optional, the body's identity, the owner its shadows carry (bit-law-v1); by default one past the disturbance types and the bodies before it
declaration.polarizer: with coupling polarizer: {family: the ray it polarizes, angle: an integer step of that family's polarization circle, pass: a unit-axial heading (+X by default), table: one entry per step of the circle in steps-ths, unpolarized: the pass share of an unpolarized ray, the table's mean by default} (ray-polarization-v1, feature 11)

external_body.does: It is a thing with declared tables (Highlights 5.4, point 22, node-is-ports-v1): its amount is its content, its identity `thing` is the owner its shadows carry, and it radiates nothing, its shadows being given with the board (`initial_field`, bit-law-v1) and circulating, a shadow that comes home to it absorbed back and released again from where it is. It never spreads (never splits, binds, unbinds, converts or decays, its whole content at one Node) and it is a border of the board: whatever thing arrives is met by its declared table, the sink by default, where it ends in the body's exact sink for its family and on the audit's absorbed_by_bodies line; whatever shadow of another thing arrives is returned on its steps, pushing the body by sign x amount x heading read as `reads` declares when its momentum_table names the shadow's family, and carrying the opposite momentum home. Its motion is caused by its momentum alone: the pushes it takes accumulate per axis and step it one Link when a whole content has accumulated, never faster than a ray, and the audit carries the bodies' momentum as its own line. On the Node it is bounded metadata: the kind, the declaration, the momentum with its accumulators and one exact sink per family; no rays, no history. It stands outside the mass ladder (hypothesis 12). When the back-reaction is wanted, a bound group with a large amount is declared instead (Highlights 3.19).
external_body.coupling_form: Under a declared coupling the body is the participant that never changes: the rule has one role that selects the body's family alone and returns it once among its outputs, and the other roles name the families it meets. Each interval the Node adds one token of the body's family (amount 1, heading +X, the body's phase) to the residents, the rule fires over the token and the arriving rays as an ordinary meeting, and the Node strips the token's output before anything leaves, requiring it back unchanged or the cycle fails. A family the rule does not name, and every returning ray, ends in the sink. In the couplings of this catalog "any" and "same" stand for the met family and "body" for the body's family; a world writes the names.

apparatus_family.name: apparatus
apparatus_family.note: The family a world gives a piece of apparatus (a mirror, a beam splitter, a phase plate, a slit, a polarizer, a wall, a screen, a beam stop) under a declared table: no clock, because the token must come back with the body's phase (clock-readings-v1: no family declares a rate); no charge and no shadows; named by no coupling but the body's own, so it is its own layer. A star or a fixed proton is a body of the ray of nature it stands for, whose shadows are given with the board.

external_body.note: Stands for a star, a neutron star, a fixed proton, a large charge or a piece of apparatus, and in a rendering carries its own picture, never mistaken for matter. Landed on 2026-09-17 as feature 7b of issue #169 (RAY_EVENT_MODEL.md, step 7); a thing with declared tables since node-is-ports-v1 (feature 17, 2026-09-18).

A1.note: The emitter is a bound clock of rate 32 at N = 256, a marked Node (a source) whose light carries its phase; the slits and the sideways sink are external bodies; the screen's marked Nodes click.

A2.note: The pair source is a marked Node emitting two light rays of one birth event; the recombiner is born_steering between the + and - Ports.

A3.note: A2 with Bob's ray held by an output-clock delay (an existing world key, not a coupling) beyond the round trip.

A4.note: The massive neutral and the massive charged families of rate 3 are the run's own declarations, not catalog rays; return_mode annul; nothing meets anything.

A5.note: The neutral control family of the same content and clock is the run's own declaration; the field of each charged family is its own shadow set (Highlights 5.4 point 12, 2026-09-18), given with the board, and the recoil is the return of the law (point 3), no coupling.

A6.note: The star is an external body of declared family and amount M at rest, its shadows the one shadow set read times the content of what is pushed (Highlights 5.4 point 18: the mass field is retired); the slow massive ray and the bound-group control series (feature 8) declare their families in the run; repeated under the law after feature 16. Under the law of the bit (2026-09-18) the star's field is its own shadow set and the recoil is the return of the law (point 3), no coupling; the delay form is deleted.

A7.note: Two bound groups of retained content M1 and M2, their families the run's declaration, and the same as two external bodies each with a coupling table reading the other's shadows times its content (point 18). Under the law of the bit (2026-09-18) the recoil is the return of the law (point 3), no coupling.

A8.note: The fixed proton is an external body of the proton family, charge +3, amount M_p, marked as a source; when its recoil is wanted it is the bound group proton under quark_binding.

A9.note: 4096 neutron groups whose weak_conversion rule declares its decay table (after_periods, clock-readings-v1); a control of 64 proton groups with no decay.

A10.note: A catalog fit, no board: the smallest electron rung k at which the muon, tau and proton ratios are integers at one N; the tau is fitted as a number, not being a catalog ray yet.

A11.note: The worlds of A1, A5 and A6 at phase_bits 75, the electron rays at the rung k of A10: a width check that the wide phase leaks into no coupling, the N of nature being the lag modulus of feature 8b (lag_bits) and not the phase circle (Highlights 3.28); under clock-readings-v1 the content / K of every thing stays below half that circle.

A12.note: Measured on 2026-09-17 (feature 11, ray-polarization-v1): the polarizer is an external body with the polarizer coupling, its table cos^2 in 256-ths; the worlds are examples/nature/a12_malus/.

A13.note: After feature 11: A2 and A3 with each analyzer a polarizer at the setting.

A14.note: One bound group of a declared massive family, either bound group of the catalog, the run's declaration, at rest and in motion by the ray_delay of feature 8.
